==============================================================================
8. STRUCTURAL INTERPRETATION
==============================================================================

Experiment 120 isolated a unique exact B-odd operator of order 3 and falling degree 2.

The coefficients were extremely large.  The present experiment tests whether that complexity is caused by the coordinate choice for the residual rows.

For a diagonal change of coordinates
    v[p,r] = w(r) q[p,r],

the operator transforms by
    F_a(r) -> F_a(r) w(r)/w(r+a).

The tested weights are standard factorial/binomial scales:
    r!, 1/r!, binom(K,r), 1/binom(K,r),
    r!(K-r)!, 1/(r!(K-r)!),
    r!/(K-r)!, (K-r)!/r!.

Three outcomes are particularly informative:
  1. a natural weight lowers the operator degree/order;
  2. a natural weight drastically reduces coefficient complexity;
  3. the transformed operator transfers exactly to another sector.

Failure of all three would strengthen the conclusion that the B-odd exceptional operator is a finite-data phenomenon rather than a disguised standard factorial/binomial transform.

All arithmetic is exact Fraction arithmetic.
No floating point.
No SymPy.
No extrapolation.
